scope: Independent source review of the opt-in guest Airbnb metadata-door continuation in tests/browser/seo-guest-acceptance.mjs.

evidence: The change's preparation record says no browser, build, or acceptance run was launched. This review also ran no browser or acceptance command.

No runtime output in this scope proves the opt-in Airbnb result, public-to-panel parity, or either outbound action. The prior Wikipedia run remains 16/17 partial evidence; this source change does not upgrade it.
verdict_a_runtime.required_for_runtime_claim: Run the guest acceptance with SEO_GUEST_METADATA_FIXTURE=airbnb and inspect its saved output; verify the actual guest panel, DOM candidates, both opened destinations, and the report status.

evidence: The change adds only an opt-in continuation guarded by the exact environment value SEO_GUEST_METADATA_FIXTURE=airbnb. With the variable unset, the Wikipedia acceptance path and existing predicates are unchanged; the new branch runs after them.

Actual product controls covered are the existing Re-audit button, existing hreflang outbound anchors in the static International group, and existing schema-type outbound anchors in the static Structured data group. SeoGroup renders as static markup; there is no expand/collapse control. The change adds no product UI control.

The expected values come from page.evaluate over the public page DOM and do not reuse the extension's audit object. It reads rel/hreflang links, JSON-LD @type values and microdata itemtype values, then compares counts, all displayed language/href pairs, schema chips, link titles/destinations, target, noopener, and noreferrer attributes.

The fixture source is sampled before and after manual re-audit and the full public evidence objects must deep-equal. The opt-in T09 pass target is added only after unique public candidates exist and both real pointer activations open tabs at their exact observed hrefs; each opened tab is closed. Missing candidates create an unverified target; assertion or navigation failures are caught as top-level unverified, never converted to pass.

The runner uses the native side-panel guest harness. The new branch navigates a public page, reads DOM, re-audits, and opens/closes public outbound tabs; it adds no sign-in, save, copy, database, or other data-write action.
limits: The acceptance oracle selects `link[rel~="alternate"][hreflang]`, while src/lib/seo/audit.ts selects `link[rel="alternate"][hreflang]`. A valid combined rel-token value can therefore appear in the independent oracle but not the collector. This is a standards/collector lead: if present, a failing assertion may expose a collector gap, not a bad oracle; the prior Airbnb fetch does not establish whether the live page has such a value.

The existing fixture report records one successful HTTP fetch with hreflang and JSON-LD candidates, but the page can vary by location or time. That report is candidate evidence, not proof the browser DOM will have usable unique candidates during the opt-in run.
This acceptance slice covers two metadata groups and their outbound links. It does not exhaust all SEO metadata, all T09 details, member/admin modes, clipboard actions, saves, or other feature cases.

controls_review.expand_collapse_controls: None are rendered by SeoGroup; no expansion behavior is claimed.

review_scope: Source-only, zero-authorship review of the target commit and its referenced fixture evidence. No browser, build, tests, auth session, data write, product edit, or push was performed.
